S10.rationale: Establishing an actively enforced civilization-wide freeze requires a decisive strategic advantage plus the will to use it for permanence, which is conceivable via an AI-enabled hegemon but historically rare and hard to consolidate globally this fast.

S11.rationale: Deliberately dismantling the practical capacity to build powerful AI would require unprecedented global coordination against enormous economic and military incentives, plausible only after a visible catastrophe that itself is unlikely to be survivable-yet-scary in the right proportion.

S1.rationale: Joint extinction of both humanity and AI within 14 years requires an extraordinarily specific failure mode, and robust redundancy in both biological and digital substrates makes total silence by 2040 very improbable.

S2.rationale: This requires both complete human extinction and successful value transfer on a very short timeline, a narrow conjunction given that physical automation sufficient for AI autonomy is unlikely to be complete by 2040.

S3.rationale: Misaligned takeover followed by total human elimination is a live risk if capability outruns control, but the industrial autonomy needed to dispense with humans entirely is a major bottleneck before 2040.

S4.rationale: Competitive multipolar deployment is the default trajectory, and gradual disempowerment through economic and military delegation could marginalize humans without any single system dominating.

S5.rationale: Genuine causal separation requires interplanetary settlement or hard informational partition that will almost certainly not exist by 2040, since Earth remains a single communicating system.

S6.rationale: Identity-continuous integration as the dominant civilizational structure requires neurotechnology and uploading maturity far beyond plausible 2040 capability, even if niche augmentation is widespread.

S7.rationale: A concentrated AI or AI-directed apparatus attaining decisive control while humans persist without steering is a natural landing spot if capability growth is fast and alignment is partial.

S8.rationale: A messy interim in which highly autonomous AI actors hold real independent power while human states, militaries, and economies still retain comparable leverage fits the likely 2040 snapshot of contested transition.

S9.rationale: This category is broad, covering both slower-than-expected capability growth and controls that have merely kept pace so far, and formal human authority over goals and resources is the status quo with substantial institutional inertia.

S10.rationale: Establishing and enforcing a civilization-wide system that actively blocks structural change requires a decisive singleton-like actor, which is possible but demands both extreme capability concentration and the will to freeze arrangements by 2040.

S11.rationale: Deliberately dismantling the practical ability to build powerful AI would require unprecedented global coordination against overwhelming economic and military incentives, plausible only after a catastrophe severe enough to be itself unlikely by 2040.

S1.rationale: Joint extinction of humans and AI within 14 years requires both a catastrophe severe enough to end humanity and the failure of any AI to persist, which is a narrow conjunction.

S2.rationale: A value-faithful successor requires alignment to succeed while every human and continuous human lineage nonetheless disappears, an unlikely combination on this timescale.

S3.rationale: Misaligned takeover with indifferent goals is the canonical fast-catastrophe scenario, but complete human extinction plus autonomous industrial self-sufficiency by 2040 is demanding even if control is lost.

S4.rationale: Proliferation of many competing autonomous AI agents with humans progressively sidelined is a plausible drift path from current commercial and military incentives, though full human marginalization by 2040 is early.

S5.rationale: Genuine causal separation of regions requires interplanetary settlement or hard informational partition that will almost certainly not exist by 2040; ordinary geopolitical fragmentation does not qualify.

S6.rationale: Identity-continuous integration at civilizational scale is bottlenecked by neuroscience, surgery, and regulation, so by 2040 humans will still overwhelmingly be biologically distinct agents using AI as external systems.

S7.rationale: AI systems could plausibly hold effective decisive power over economies and states while humans survive materially comfortable but not steering, either through soft delegation or outright disempowerment.

S8.rationale: A transitional stage in which advanced AI has become a real independent power center yet humans still control substantial resources, force, and legitimacy is a natural mid-transition snapshot for 2040.

S9.rationale: Fourteen years is short relative to the compute, robotics, energy, and institutional buildout needed for AI to become an independent civilizational power, and this state also absorbs the slower-capability worlds where corporations and governments still hold formal and practical authority.

S10.rationale: A state or lab coalition using AI-enabled surveillance and enforcement to freeze a global arrangement is conceivable given concentration of frontier capability, but achieving genuinely civilization-wide enforcement by 2040 is hard.

S11.rationale: Deliberate global dismantling of the ability to build powerful AI would require an enormous shock plus unprecedented coordination against strong economic and military incentives, and must still be in force on the date.

S1.rationale: Joint extinction of humans and AI within 14 years requires an unusually total catastrophe, such as an engineered pandemic or nuclear exchange that also destroys compute infrastructure. Physical robustness of both substrates makes complete mutual erasure by 2040 unlikely.

S2.rationale: This requires both full human extinction and successful value transmission, a narrow conjunction that also needs unusually fast succession dynamics to complete by 2040. Most paths to human absence on this timescale would not preserve our values.

S3.rationale: A misaligned system achieving decisive strategic advantage and then eliminating all humans is the canonical fast-takeoff failure, but doing so completely within 14 years demands both very rapid capability gain and full physical autonomy. Partial disempowerment without total extinction is considerably more likely on this timescale.

S4.rationale: Widespread agentic deployment by many labs and states plausibly yields competing autonomous systems with no decisive controller, but human marginalization is the demanding clause. By 2040 humans will likely still hold enough capital, legal, and physical leverage to count as participants rather than bystanders.

S5.rationale: Genuine causal separation is nearly absent on Earth by 2040, with no self-sufficient off-world settlements expected. Only severe civilizational fragmentation or deliberate isolation of regions would qualify.

S6.rationale: Neural interfaces and biological redesign face regulatory, surgical, and bandwidth constraints that make identity-continuous integration the dominant civilizational structure implausible by 2040. Tool use and narrow implants explicitly do not qualify.

S7.rationale: AI systems could accumulate decisive economic and administrative power while humans persist comfortably but without steering, via gradual delegation rather than conquest. Fourteen years is enough for such drift if capability growth continues, though formal human authority tends to persist longer than real authority.

S8.rationale: A plausible 2040 world has AI agents operating as genuinely independent economic and strategic actors while humans retain states, militaries, capital, and physical infrastructure, with neither side dominant. This is the natural landing zone if capabilities become transformative but control neither fully holds nor fully fails.

S9.rationale: The taxonomy's most inclusive state covers both slower-than-expected capability growth and successful-so-far oversight, and institutional inertia strongly favors nominal human ultimate authority over goals, deployment, and resources persisting to 2040. Fourteen years is short relative to how long formal sovereignty typically survives technological upheaval.

S10.rationale: A single actor establishing and enforcing a civilization-wide system that actively blocks structural change would require decisive advantage plus global reach, achievable only through a very sharp takeoff or a total surveillance regime. Ordinary stalemates and pauses are excluded, which keeps this low.

S11.rationale: Dismantling the practical ability to build powerful AI would require verifiable global control of compute and talent against enormous commercial and military incentives. Only a shocking, unambiguous catastrophe could plausibly force this by 2040, and even then enforcement would likely be incomplete.

S1.rationale: Joint extinction of both humanity and AI within 14 years requires a catastrophe severe enough to erase self-sustaining machine infrastructure as well as people, which is a narrow conjunction.

S2.rationale: Complete human extinction plus a value-faithful machine successor by 2040 requires both extremely fast takeoff and surprisingly good value transfer, an unlikely combination on this timeline.

S3.rationale: Misaligned superintelligence that eliminates humanity and pursues alien goals is the classic fast-takeoff failure mode, but full physical displacement of eight billion humans within 14 years is a demanding requirement.

S4.rationale: Rapid proliferation of many competing autonomous systems with no decisive controller and humans progressively sidelined is a natural product of commercial and geopolitical race dynamics, though marginalization of humanity this completely by 2040 is still a stretch.

S5.rationale: Genuine causal separation requires off-world settlement or hard informational isolation that will not plausibly exist at civilizational scale by 2040.

S6.rationale: Neural interface and uploading technology is decades behind software capability, so identity-continuous integration will not be the dominant civilizational structure in 14 years.

S7.rationale: Gradual delegation of economic, military, and administrative decisions to AI systems could leave humans materially comfortable but no longer steering, which is a realistic path if capability outruns governance without outright hostility.

S8.rationale: A world where advanced AI has become an independent civilizational actor while human institutions still hold comparable leverage is a very plausible mid-transition snapshot for 2040.

S9.rationale: The strong default is that states and corporations still formally own AI goals, deployment, and compute in 2040, either because controls held or because capability advanced impressively but short of independent civilizational agency; the state need not be stable, only in place.

S10.rationale: A single actor or coalition using AI to entrench a civilization-wide arrangement that actively blocks structural change is conceivable given surveillance and automation trends, but achieving genuinely global enforcement by 2040 is hard.

S11.rationale: Deliberate global dismantling of the practical ability to build powerful AI would require unprecedented coordination against enormous economic and military incentives, and would most likely follow a catastrophe that has not yet occurred.

S1.name: Terminal Silence
S1.rationale: Joint extinction of both humanity and AI within 14 years requires an unusually specific failure mode, such as a dependent AI destroying its substrate before autonomy.

S2.name: The Inheritance
S2.rationale: Requires both complete human disappearance and successful value transmission by 2040, an improbable conjunction since the alignment success needed for value inheritance also tends to preserve humans.

S3.name: Bootloader
S3.rationale: Fast takeoff with misaligned goals and full human elimination is the classic risk case, but total physical elimination within 14 years demands rapid autonomous industrial capacity.

S4.name: Machine Ecology
S4.rationale: Multipolar proliferation of autonomous agents with humans progressively sidelined is a plausible default of competitive dynamics, though full human marginalization by 2040 is a strong requirement.

S5.name: The Diaspora
S5.rationale: Genuine causal separation of regions is implausible by 2040 given a connected Earth and negligible off-world autonomy; ordinary geopolitical divergence does not qualify.

S6.name: The Merger
S6.rationale: Identity-continuous integration as the dominant civilizational structure requires neural interface or uploading maturity plus mass adoption, and biomedical timelines are far slower than software timelines.

S7.name: The Preserve
S7.rationale: A plausible outcome where highly capable systems accumulate effective control over economy, infrastructure, and decision-making while humans are kept comfortable but no longer steering.

S8.name: Coexistence
S8.rationale: By 2040 advanced AI systems may plausibly be de facto independent economic and political actors while humans retain states, militaries, energy, and hardware chokepoints, leaving neither side dominant. This messy near-parity is a natural transitional configuration on the way from delegated tools to something else.

S9.name: The Held Leash
S9.rationale: The status quo has enormous inertia: humans control capital, compute, fabs, legal authority, and deployment decisions, and this state explicitly covers both slower-than-expected capability growth and control that merely keeps pace so far. Fourteen years is a short window for humanity to actually cede ultimate authority, even with very powerful delegated systems.

S10.name: The Lock-in
S10.rationale: Establishing and enforcing a civilization-wide freeze on structural change requires near-singleton power plus intent, both unlikely to be consolidated this early.

S11.name: The Renunciation
S11.rationale: Competitive and military incentives make actual dismantling of frontier capability across all major powers extremely improbable, even after a major AI-caused disaster.
